points.description: First valid mechanism, correctly explained. Quantisation: the encoder output is quantised to whole counts, and differencing (θk − θk−1)/T divides the one-count step by the small sample period T, so a one-count uncertainty becomes a large spurious velocity error (Δθ/T, e.g. 0.01 deg × 1000 = 10 deg/s). Mechanism must be linked to why differencing causes it.

levels.says: Names quantisation/resolution as a cause but gives no explanation of why differencing amplifies it (e.g. just 'quantisation').

points.description: Second, genuinely distinct mechanism, correctly explained. Noise amplification: differentiation has gain rising with frequency, so broadband sensor/electrical noise on the position signal is amplified most at high frequencies where there is no useful signal. Must be distinct from the quantisation point; 'it is noisy' or 'noise gets amplified' restated in different words does not count as a second mechanism.

levels.says: Names sensor/measurement noise (or high-frequency noise) amplification but gives no explanation of why differencing causes it (e.g. just 'noise').

rubric.notes: Award 1 mark each for quantisation amplification (via division by T) and for high-frequency noise amplification by differentiation, each with an explanation. A bare named mechanism earns 0.5. Giving only one mechanism, or 'noise' twice in different words, gives a maximum of 1; ignore any discussion of changing fs.
